title: Serial UART & Wireless Communication
summary: Connect Arduinos to computers, Bluetooth modules, and GPS with asynchronous TX/RX serial streams.

steps.title: Asynchronous Streams
steps.markdownContent: UART serial needs no shared clock line! Both devices simply agree on a common speed (the **Baud Rate**, such as 9600 or 115200 bits per second).

steps.title: Crossed Wires: TX to RX
steps.markdownContent: Always cross serial wires: Arduino's `TX` (Transmit) connects to the peripheral's `RX` (Receive), and peripheral `TX` connects to Arduino `RX`!

steps.title: SoftwareSerial for Modules
steps.markdownContent: Pins 0 and 1 are used by the USB cable for programming. To talk to Bluetooth (HC-05), we use the `<SoftwareSerial.h>` library on pins 10 and 11!

steps.title: UART Checkpoint
steps.markdownContent: What happens if two devices attempt to communicate with mismatched baud rates (e.g. 9600 vs 115200)?
